objective: Computation and proof by example. Signed Z4 (x +- y +- z +- w = c) fails globally on a 6-point 4-regular substrate and keeps a knot after removing any line (brute force); signed Z4 at three places fails globally on a 9-point cubic substrate and keeps a knot after removing a line (brute force), while on all 60 cubic substrates up to 8 points its global failures are rigid. Unit-weighted Z8, Z9, Z25, Z27 laws have non-rigid global failures on many cubic census substrates. Every non-rigid failure has a non-cyclic solution group.
status: Proved by RIGID-SELECTION-20261101-001B-P001: signed Z4 fails globally and keeps knots after every line removal on the 6-point four-place substrate (complements of a hexagon's edges), and after one removal on a 9-point cubic substrate; on all 73 connected cubic substrates with at most 8 points its global failures are rigid under every signing class, so 9 points is the minimum at three places; unit-weighted Z8, Z9, Z25, Z27 keep knots on many census substrates; every kept knot sits in a non-cyclic solution group. So composing like cycles does not force rigid selection
title: Global failures that keep a knot
